newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - July 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- An amnesty applicant for the St James church massacre was "a guest" of the Pan Africanist Congress (PAC) and "could not be released" as a protest against the commission's lack of objectivity, the PAC said on Thursday.

- Former strockbroking director Gerrit Steenkamp pleaded guilty before a disciplinary committee on Thursday to the misappropriation of about 5 million rand in client funds between August 1994 and April this year, the SA Institute of Stockbrokers said last night.

- Gold Fields of South Africa kicked off the SA gold industry's June quarterly results on an ominous note on Thursday, posting an 18.6 percent decline in aggregate taxed profit to 192.3 million rand and raising the spectre of mine closures.

- Hot on the heels of its fake degrees scam, the University of Zululand has uncovered a second fraudulent scheme in which at least 640,000 rand was falsely credited to students' accounts, relieving them of fees owed and other debts.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Chris Stals, the Reserve Bank governor, said on Thursday that only 25 million rand had left South Africa after the relaxation of exchange controls on July 1.

- The manufacturing sector shed another 14,000 jobs during the first quarter of this year, despite a 19 percent increase in the manufacturing production index during the same period, the Central Statistical Service (CSS) said on Thursday.

- Despite higher production, the weak bullion price knocked the June quarter gold earnings of Gold Fields of South Africa, the mining house. However, the 18.6 percent fall in profits was not as bad as expected, the company said on Thursday.
- Network Healthcare Holdings (NetCare) was on the verge of signing a 950 million rand deal to buy 67 percent of Clinic Holdings, industry sources said on Thursday.
- National Sorghum Breweries is losing market share to rival Traditional Beer Investments, the sorghum beer brewing subsidiary of South African Breweries, according to sales figures.
SAKE BEELD
- The Leeudoorn gold mines, a part of Kloof gold mines company near Carltonville, is in danger of being closed. The mine employs about 5,000 people.
- The Provision of employment in manufacturing and construction sectors dropped further in March.
THE STAR

- Dawie Ackermann, his eyes red-rimmed, his eyelashes wet with tears and his voice shaky with emotion, asked the three men who this week admitted to having been part of the gang that killed his wife to turn around in their seats and face him.
- South African prostitutes, who for years were relentlessly hunted down by the police's morality and vice squads, can now call on the "boys in blue" to be their guardian angels.
- Nigeria has warned the Commonwealth and the international community of grave consequences should the Commonwealth Ministerial Action Group adopt measures against the country's interests.

- The Vaal Dam hippo must go. That was the message that came through loud and clear at a meeting in Oranjeville, where it was stressed that it was only a matter of time before the town's adopted pet was provoked into an attack.
